name: Sentence Fragment Detection
description: Analyzes the text for the presence of deliberate sentence fragments—sentences that lack a main clause, subject, or finite verb. Large Language Models are heavily penalized during training for producing grammatically incomplete sentences. As a result, they almost exclusively output perfectly formed, textbook-compliant subject-verb-object structures. Human writers, especially in creative, persuasive, or conversational contexts, frequently deploy deliberate sentence fragments for stylistic emphasis, sharp pacing, or emotional impact (e.g., 'Not exactly.', 'A complete disaster.', 'Because why not?').
algorithm: Dependency Parsing for Headless Syntax Trees
mechanism: The algorithm parses the syntactic structure of every sentence using a dependency parser. It specifically hunts for sentences that fail to resolve to a 'ROOT' verb or lack a foundational subject-predicate relationship (headless syntax trees). If a document contains zero or near-zero fragments across a large volume of text, it strongly indicates the rigid grammatical compliance typical of an AI model. Conversely, the presence of well-placed, intentional fragments heavily weights the text toward human authorship.
useCase: Highly effective for auditing blogs, op-eds, marketing copy, and creative writing where human authors naturally employ varied, non-standard punctuation and fragmented syntax for rhetorical effect.
strengths:
• Exceptional at identifying human writing (reducing false positives), as AI models simply do not naturally generate stylistic fragments without highly specific, unnatural prompting.
• Works well on modern digital communication styles (emails, social media) where fragmented writing is the norm.
limitations:
• Provides little signal on highly formal academic or legal texts, as humans also strictly avoid fragments in those domains.
• Very short texts may randomly contain no fragments, rendering the metric statistically insignificant.
parameters:
Analysis: Syntactic Dependency Parsing and Root Verb Extraction
Metric: Frequency of Grammatically Incomplete Sentences
Output: 0-100 Strict Grammatical Compliance (Artificiality) Score
accuracy: Moderate — 68-75% accuracy. Its primary value is as a 'human-indicator'; the presence of fragments strongly implies a human, though the absence does not guarantee an AI.

references.title: Uchendu, A. et al. (2020). Authorship Attribution for Neural Text Generation. EMNLP.
Jurafsky, D. & Martin, J.H. (2024). Speech and Language Processing. 3rd Edition.
